papers.title: Avoiding Distances
papers.abstract: Given a finite planar point set $X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$, let $a_1<a_2< \cdots < a_s$ denote the $s \leq {n \choose 2}$ different (Euclidean) distances between points in $X$. The aim is to retain as many of the points as possible such that certain imposed inter-pair distances are avoided. For example, we show that: (A) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, an independent set of size $0.2293 n$ in the unit distance graph determined by $X$ can be found in $O(n^2)$ time. For any fixed $k \in \mathbf{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that for any set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, and set $D$ of size $k$, there exists a subset $X' \subseteq X$ of size $|X'| \geq c_k |X|$ in which no pair of points is at some distance in $D$ (we say that $X'$ avoids distances in $D$). Such a set can be found efficiently. (B) (i) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/2$ that avoids the maximum distance; this bound cannot be improved. (ii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $8n/47$ that avoids both the minimum and maximum distance; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $5n/16$ points can be retained with this property. (iii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/7$ whose diameter is at most half the original diameter; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $n/6$ points can be retained with this property. (C) (i) For any $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation for \textsc{MIS} in the minimum distance graph of $n$ points in the plane can be found in $2^{O(1/\varepsilon)} n^{O(1)}$ time. (ii) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, a maximum independent set in the graph of diameters can be computed in $O(n^2)$ time. The techniques used to handle the planar case can be extended to $\mathbf{R}^d$ for any fixed dimension $d$.

papers.title: When Are Monomial Symmetric Polynomials Hard?
papers.abstract: For a partition $\boldsymbol{\lambda} = (\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)$ and $n\ge r$, the monomial symmetric polynomial is defined as $$m_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}(x_1,\ldots,x_n) := \sum x_{i_1}^{\lambda_1} x_{i_2}^{\lambda_2} \cdots x_{i_r}^{\lambda_r},$$ where the sum ranges over all distinct monomials obtained by assigning the parts of $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$ to pairwise distinct variables. We establish an almost-complete dichotomy for the complexity of the monomial symmetric polynomials $m_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$: If a family of partitions contains polynomially many distinct parts, then the corresponding monomial symmetric polynomials (on sufficiently many variables) are VNP-complete. If the number of distinct parts is constant, the family admits polynomial-size circuits. Thus the only remaining gap concerns the intermediate regime where the number of distinct parts grows subpolynomially. As part of our proof, we use combinatorial properties of matching polynomials to establish VNP-hardness of the perfect matching polynomial for blow-up graphs; these are graphs with non-generic edge-weights that are obtained by "blowing up" a smaller graph. We reduce these matching polynomials to monomial-symmetric polynomials by combining classical techniques from algebraic complexity theory with structural properties of Sidon sets.

papers.title: Almost Empty Monochromatic Polygons in Planar Point Sets
papers.abstract: For integers $r \ge 3$, $c \ge 2$, and $s \ge 0$, let $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,s)$ denote the smallest integer such that any set of at least $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,s)$ points in the plane in general position (no three on a line), colored with $c$ colors, contains a monochromatic $r$-gon (not necessarily convex) with at most $s$ interior points. Define $\lambda_r^{\star}(c)$ to be the smallest integer such that $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,\lambda_r^{\star}(c)) < \infty$. The case of triangles, that is, $r=3$, has been studied in recent years. In this paper, we establish bounds on $\lambda_r^{\star}(c)$, for $r \ge 4$. Specifically, in the bichromatic case, we prove that $\lambda_r^{\star}(2)\leq \lfloor\frac{r-2}{2}\rfloor$, for every $r\geq3$. For hexagons, we sharpen this bound to $\lambda_6^{\star}(2)\leq1$, that is, every sufficiently large bichromatic planar point set in general position contains a monochromatic hexagon with at most one interior point. Next, for any number of colors $c\geq3$ and $r\geq3$, we show that $$(r - 2) \left \lfloor \frac{c-1}{2} \right \rfloor \leq \lambda_r^\star(c) \leq (r-2)(c-2)+\left\lfloor(r-2)\delta_c\right\rfloor, $$ for some constant $\delta_c \in (0, \frac{1}{2}]$, depending on $c$. The upper bounds combine spiral polygonizations with nested convex-hull arguments and, in the hexagon case, incidence counting in $4$-connected triangulations. The lower bounds follow from colored Horton-set constructions.

papers.title: Approximating Independent Sets Using Additive Combinatorics
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic quasi-polynomial time algorithm for approximating the largest independent set in a graph. We show that if an $N$-vertex graph contains an independent set of size $2^{-t} N$, then we can find an independent set of size $2^t$ in quasi-polynomial time, for all $t$ up to a constant factor of $(\log N)^{1/3}$. This gives an approximation factor of $N / \exp((\log N)^{1/3})$, which has the same shape as known hardness results for quasi-polynomial time algorithms, up to a different exponent of the logarithm. The algorithm builds on a structural principle: a graph containing a large independent set must also contain a large sparse structured set, and such a set can be found efficiently. A greedy algorithm then extracts an independent set from it. Our proof draws on tools in additive combinatorics, in particular spreadness and sifting, to obtain the combinatorial structural results. We then convert these to efficient algorithms using pseudo-marginals obtained by semidefinite programming.

papers.title: Cyclic Equalizability Characterized by Parikh Vectors
papers.abstract: Cyclic equalizability is a notion introduced by Shinagawa and Nuida in 2025, in the study of card-based cryptography. Informally, a collection of words is cyclically equalizable if, by inserting the same letters at the same positions in all words, they can be transformed into words that are cyclic shifts of one another. Shinagawa and Nuida showed that two binary words of equal length are cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Hamming weight. They also posed the problem of characterizing cyclic equalizability over larger alphabets. In this paper, we completely characterize cyclic equalizability for two words over an arbitrary finite alphabet by proving that two words are cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Parikh vector.

papers.title: Two characterizations of chain partitioned probe graphs
papers.abstract: Chain graphs are exactly bipartite graphs without induced $2K_2$ (a graph with four vertices and two disjoint edges). A graph $G=(V,E)$ with a given independent set $S\subseteq V$ (a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices) is said to be a chain partitioned probe graph if $G$ can be extended to a chain graph by adding edges between certain vertices in $S$. %there exists a set $E'\subseteq\binom{S}{2}$ such that the graph $G'=(V,E\cup E')$ is a chain graph. In this note we give two characterizations for chain partitioned probe graphs. The first one describes chain partitioned probe graphs by six forbidden subgraphs. The second one characterizes these graphs via a certain ``enhanced graph'': $G$ is a chain partitioned probe graph if and only if the enhanced graph $G^*$ is a chain graph. This is analogous to a result on interval (respectively, chordal, threshold, trivially perfect) partitioned probe graphs, and gives an $O(m^2)$-time recognition algorithm for chain partitioned probe graphs.

papers.title: A simplified proof of the FPRAS for counting perfect matchings
papers.abstract: We give a simplified, self-contained proof of OpenAI's FPRAS for counting perfect matchings in general graphs. As in the original proof, we use a restricted Poincar\'e inequality for two matchings to sample weighted perfect matchings and estimate their total weight. We simplify the proof of this inequality by isolating parts of alternating cycles directly on the original vertex set and controlling the resulting error terms. This avoids the auxiliary vertices and tree constructions used in the original proof. The argument preserves the required parameter bounds and yields the same FPRAS guarantee.

papers.title: Unranking $S$-avoiding permutations with two forbidden offsets
papers.abstract: Given a finite family of combinatorial objects with a total order, ranking asks for the position of a given object, and unranking asks for the object occupying a given position. Both provide algorithmic access to families too large to enumerate. Kagey gave a polynomial-time algorithm for several position-restricted families and left open the case of $\{-1,1\}$-avoiding permutations. We show that when $|S| = 2$, the graph of forbidden squares is $2$-regular, a disjoint union of cycles, and that fixing a prefix leaves only paths and untouched cycles. This yields polynomial-time prefix counting, ranking and unranking for every two-element set of offsets, covering $\{-1,1\}$. The same structure gives a short proof that the number of $\{-1,1\}$-avoiding permutations equals the $n$-th m\'enage number for odd $n$ and exceeds it by $2$ for even $n$, proving a conjecture recorded in the OEIS entry A354152.

papers.title: The Kemeny-Braess Paradox in Random Graphs
papers.abstract: In 2016, Kirkland and Zeng initiated the mathematical treatment of Braess paradox for random walks on graphs using Kemeny's constant as the measure of travel time. We study this phenomenon for the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$. An edge in a connected graph is called Kemeny-Braess if its deletion preserves connectedness and decreases Kemeny's constant, while a nonedge is Kemeny-Braess if its insertion increases Kemeny's constant. Let $\bar d=(n-1)p$ be the expected degree of $G\sim G(n,p)$, and assume that $\bar d-\log n\to\infty$, so that $G$ is connected with high probability. We determine the sharp asymptotic thresholds for the existence of both types of paradoxical behaviour. With $C^*=1/(1-\log 2)$, the threshold for Kemeny-Braess edges is $\bar d=C^*\log n$, whereas the threshold for Kemeny-Braess nonedges is $\bar d=2C^*\log n$. Hence, as the expected degree $\bar d$ increases, the connected regime exhibits three phases: first Kemeny-Braess paradox occurs for both edges and nonedges, then only for nonedges, and finally it disappears. In particular, in the dense regime, with high probability $G$ has no Kemeny-Braess edges or nonedges. This contrasts sharply with the spectral gap of the normalised Laplacian, for which Braess' paradox persists at constant edge density. Our proof combines a spectral-moment expansion of Kemeny's constant with uniform edge-perturbation estimates. Near the thresholds, the sign of the perturbation is governed by the endpoint degrees, and binomial large deviations yield the constant $C^*$ and the factor of two between the two thresholds.

papers.title: Erd\H{o}s-Gy\'arf\'as Balanced Five-Colorings
papers.abstract: A coloring of the edges of a complete graph with $r$ colors is balanced if the edges among any $r+1$ vertices use all $r$ colors. Erd\H{o}s and Gy\'arf\'as (1999) conjectured that for all $r\ge3$ the complete graph $K_{r^2+1}$ has no balanced $r$-coloring. They proved the conjecture for $r=3$ and $r=4$. We prove the conjecture for $r=5$, the first new case settled in over two decades. There is no balanced $5$-coloring of $K_{26}$, and since $K_{25}$ has one, $K_{25}$ is the largest complete graph admitting a balanced $5$-coloring. We design a reduce--dispatch--enumerate workflow, where every machine step produces an artifact that can be independently checked. First, we use a machine-checked (Lean 4) proof to reduce the conjecture to a single extremal statement about the color class with the fewest edges: no graph on $26$ vertices has between $55$ and $65$ edges while every $6$ of its vertices span between $1$ and $11$ edges. We then search on the sparse class instead of its dense complement, which makes enumeration up to isomorphism feasible. With classical stability theorems for $K_6$-free graphs, we dispatch the five near-extremal edge counts analytically. For the exhaustive enumeration on the remaining six edge counts, we design efficient encodings with SAT modulo symmetries and parallel cube-and-conquer. We also certify all eleven edge counts: each of the $12{,}296$ subproblems carries a clausal refutation checked by the independent verifier drat-trim, and all $273{,}503{,}938$ symmetry-breaking clauses are also validated against the vertex permutations that justify them.

papers.title: Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces
papers.abstract: A single-track Gray code of length $n$ is a cyclic Gray code of $n$-bit words in which every column is a cyclic shift of the first. For prime $n$ the longest possible period is $2^n-2$. Whether it is attained for every prime has been open since Hiltgen, Paterson and Brandestini introduced these codes in 1996, and optimal codes were known for primes $n\le 19$. We show that a conjecture of Degni and Drisko (2007) on the reflected Gray code order of necklaces implies optimal single-track Gray codes for every prime. Their list of necklaces, conjecturally a Gray path for prime $n$, closes into a Hamilton cycle of the necklace graph after $(n-3)/2$ explicit P\'osa rotations, and such a cycle lifts to an optimal code. This implication is formalized in Lean 4. Together with computation it gives optimal single-track Gray codes for every odd prime $n\le 47$: for $n\le 37$ explicit codes checked word by word by a program independent of the generator, and for $n=41$, $43$ and $47$ codes obtained from the implication after the Degni-Drisko property was verified at these lengths by two independently written programs.

papers.title: On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs
papers.abstract: We propose and study a multi-labeling generalization of the $k$-radio labeling problem of graphs: given a graph $G$ and integers $k$ and $m$, assign to each vertex of $G$ a set of $m$ integer labels such that distinct labels assigned to a vertex differ by at least $k+1$, and the labels of any two distinct vertices $x$ and $y$ pairwise differ by at least $k+1-d(x,y)$, with $d(x,y)$ being the distance between vertices $x$ and $y$. We prove general bounds on the minimum span of such a labeling and more refined results for the case $k=1$. For paths and cycles, we derive sharp bounds on the minimum span when $k$ is small. We finally propose a conjecture for the minimum span on the path and for an almost-tight bound on the cycle.

papers.title: Invitation to torso parameters of annotated graphs
papers.abstract: An annotated graph is a pair $(G,S)$, where $G$ is a graph and $S$ is a subset of vertices of $G$. We present a unified approach for definitions of annotated versions of classical graph parameters such as treewidth, pathwidth, treedepth, etc. A generic way to incorporate a distinguished set of vertices into a graph parameter is via torsos. Given a graph $G$ and a subset $S'\subseteq V(G)$, we define $\mathrm{torso}_G(S')$ to be the graph with vertex set $S'$ in which distinct vertices $u,v\in S'$ are adjacent if and only if there exists a $u$-$v$ path in $G$ whose internal vertices lie outside $S'$. Now let $\mathrm{p}$ be any graph parameter. For an annotated graph $(G,S)$, we define the torso $\mathrm{p}$ of $(G,S)$ by \[\mathrm{p}(G,S) = \min\{\mathrm{p}(\mathrm{torso}_G(S')) \mid S \subset S' \subset V(G)\}.\] For a minor-closed class of annotated graphs $\mathcal{C}$, we discuss equivalent conditions for $\mathrm{p}(G,S)$ bounded for all $(G,S)\in\mathcal{C}$ in terms of annotated graphs excluded in $\mathcal{C}$. In many cases, we collect known results from the literature. We include two new arguments for $\mathrm{p}$ being the $2$-treedepth and the feedback vertex number. Among other statements, we also include a variant of the Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property for annotated cycles. We propose some new research directions.

papers.title: Ramsey expansions of $S$-metric spaces
papers.abstract: Let $S\subseteq \mathbb R^+$ be a subset of positive reals. We say that a metric space is an $S$-metric space if the range of the metric is a subset of $S\cup \{0\}$. In 2007, Delhomm\'{e}, Laflamme, Pouzet, and Sauer characterized those sets $S$ for which the class of all finite $S$-metric spaces has the amalgamation property. Given an amalgamation class, a natural question is what its Ramsey expansion is. Ramsey expansions are known for classes of $S$-metric spaces for which $S\cup\{0\}$ carries a natural distance monoid structure, for example for $S=\mathbb Q^+$ or when $S$ is topologically closed. In this paper, we extend this result to all amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces, thereby completing the Ramsey-theoretic classification of amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces.

papers.title: The rank of the random $k$-XORSAT matrix beyond satisfiability
papers.abstract: The random $k$-XORSAT matrix is an $m\times n$ random matrix $\mathbf A$ over $\mathbb F_2$ that represents a random instance of the $k$-XORSAT problem. Each row of $\mathbf A$ contains precisely $k\geq3$ non-zero entries in random positions. The rows are drawn independently. The matrix $\mathbf A$ is known to have full row rank for $m/n$ below the random $k$-XORSAT satisfiability threshold, which is known explicitly [Dubois, Mandler~2002; Pittel, Sorkin~2016]. Motivated by a problem from quantum game theory and refining a result of Cooper, Frieze and Pegden (2019), we determine the limiting distribution of the rank of $\mathbf A$ beyond the satisfiability threshold.

papers.title: An Algebraic Approach to Periodicity and Complexity of Delone Sets
papers.abstract: We study the connection between local complexity and periodicity of Delone sets using an algebraic approach based on annihilators, that is, finite linear relations between translations of a configuration. We model colored Delone sets (Delone multisets) as $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations, that is, functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite range, and extend the notions of annihilators and periodizers from $\mathbb{Z}^d$-configurations to the geometric setting of Delone sets. Our main results describe the structure imposed by the existence of non-trivial annihilators. We show that any $\mathbb{R}^d$-configuration admitting non-trivial annihilators has an annihilator of a particularly simple form, namely a product of finitely many difference operators corresponding to translations in pairwise rationally independent directions. We further improve this result and prove that for configurations supported on Delone sets of finite local complexity (FLC), the corresponding directions can be chosen pairwise linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$. As a consequence of the existence of the special annihilator, we show that $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations with annihilators admit a decomposition into finitely many components that are periodic in pairwise rationally independent directions. Moreover, we connect local complexity with algebraic structure by proving that Meyer sets with sufficiently slow patch complexity growth have low pattern complexity and hence admit non-trivial annihilators. Finally, we establish a sufficient and necessary condition under which the existence of suitable annihilators forces periodicity of $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations supported on FLC Delone sets.

papers.title: Solution to a problem on isolation of $3$-vertex paths
papers.abstract: The $3$-path isolation number of a connected $n$-vertex graph $G$, denoted by $\iota(G,P_3)$, is the size of a smallest subset $D$ of the vertex set of $G$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ intersects the vertex sets of the $3$-vertex paths of $G$, meaning that no two edges of $G-N[D]$ intersect. Zhang and Wu proved that $\iota(G,P_3) \leq 2n/7$ unless $G$ is a $3$-path or a $3$-cycle or a $6$-cycle. The bound is attained by infinitely many graphs having induced $6$-cycles. Huang, Zhang and Jin proved that if $G$ has no $6$-cycles, or $G$ has no induced $5$-cycles and no induced $6$-cycles, then $\iota(G, P_3) \leq n/4$ unless $G$ is a $3$-path or a $3$-cycle or a $7$-cycle or an $11$-cycle. They asked if the bound still holds asymptotically for connected graphs having no induced $6$-cycles. More precisely, taking $f(n)$ to be the maximum value of $\iota(G,P_3)$ over all connected $n$-vertex graphs $G$ having no induced $6$-cycles, their question is whether $\limsup_{n \to\infty}\frac{f(n)}{n} = \frac{1}{4}$. We verify this by proving that $f(n) = \left \lfloor (n+1)/4 \right \rfloor$. Therefore, induced $6$-cycles solely account for the jump to the bound $2n/7$. The proof hinges on further proving that if $G$ is such a graph and $\iota(G, P_3) = (n+1)/4$, then $\iota(G-v, P_3) < \iota(G, P_3)$ for each vertex $v$ of $G$. This new idea promises to be of further use. We also prove that if the maximum degree of such a graph $G$ is at least $5$, then $\iota(G,P_3) \leq n/4$.

papers.title: Subexponential upper bound on the number of rich words
papers.abstract: Let $R_q(n)$ denote the number of rich words of length $n$ over a fixed alphabet of size $q\geq2$. It is known that $R_q(n)^{1/n}\to1$. We establish a nonrecursive subexponential upper bound on the number of rich words, with its asymptotic growth quantified in terms of an iterated logarithm. For every $\lambda\in(1/2,1)$ and $\gamma>1$, there exists $c>0$ such that, for every positive function $\phi$ satisfying $\phi(n)\to\infty$ and $n/\phi(n)\to\infty$, the functions \[ f(n)=\left[c\ln^{*}\!\left(\frac{n}{\phi(n)}\ln q\right)\right]^{1/\gamma}, \qquad B(n)=q^{\frac{n}{\phi(n)}+\frac{n}{(2\lambda)^{f(n)-1}}} \] satisfy $R_q(n)\leq B(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and $B(n)^{1/n}\to1$. Here $\ln^{*}$ is the iterated natural logarithm, with value zero on $(0,1]$. The proof iterates a counting inequality based on palindromic factorization and controls the resulting multiplicative constants using the iterated logarithm.

papers.title: Excluding an apex-forest or a fan as quickly as possible
papers.abstract: We show that every graph $G$ excluding an apex-forest $H$ as a minor has layered pathwidth at most $|V(H)|-2$, and that every graph $G$ excluding an apex-linear forest (such as a fan) $H$ as a minor has layered treedepth at most $|V(H)|-2$. We further show that both bounds are optimal. These results improve on recent results of Hodor, La, Micek, and Rambaud (2025): The first result improves the previous best-known bound by a multiplicative factor of $2$, while the second strengthens a previous quadratic bound. In addition, we reduce from quadratic to linear the bound on the $S$-focused treedepth $\mathrm{td}(G,S)$ for graphs $G$ with a prescribed set of vertices $S$ excluding models of paths in which every branch set intersects $S$.

papers.title: New Maximum Hermitian $d$-Codes and New Invariants from Skew Polynomial Rings
papers.abstract: Maximum rank-distance codes were introduced independently by Delsarte (1978) and Gabidulin (1985) for unrestricted matrix spaces, and their study was subsequently extended to the classical form spaces of alternating, symmetric, and Hermitian matrices. For Hermitian $d$-codes, Schmidt (2018) established the upper bound and constructed optimal additive codes for all admissible parameters except when $n$ and $d$ are both even and $4\le d\le n-2$. We settle this final open existence case, more generally, construct additive maximum Hermitian rank-metric codes for every admissible length and minimum distance. Rather than working directly in the space of Hermitian matrices, we construct our objects within central simple algebras with unitary involution arising from quotients of skew polynomial rings. We also introduce scalar-field and Lyapunov operators in these algebras, leading to new invariants for the equivalence of additive Hermitian codes. Explicitly determining these invariants yields strong necessary conditions for Hermitian equivalence and demonstrates that our construction contains a large number of pairwise inequivalent codes.

papers.title: New lower bounds for binary constant-weight codes from prescribed-automorphism search, and two quantum codes meeting their upper bounds
papers.abstract: We give explicit binary constant-weight codes that raise the lower bounds on $A(n,6,w)$ in eight cells of Brouwer's table, all now listed there. The first round (9 October 2026) gave four values: $A(27,6,11)\ge 19305$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24453$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 18642$ and $A(28,6,9)\ge 11154$, together with an explicit $A(24,6,12)$ code of 5566 words, now in the table's list of lost codes. The second round (14 October 2026) gave seven values, listed in the table since 15 October 2026: $A(29,6,10)\ge 27183$, $A(29,6,11)\ge 42042$, $A(29,6,9)\ge 14781$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 19110$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24804$, $A(28,6,9)\ge 11388$ and $A(27,6,13)\ge 27783$, three of which replace first-round values. Every code is a union of orbits of the semilinear affine group $\mathrm{A\Gamma L}(1,27)$, its index-2 subgroup, or $\mathrm{AGL}(1,23)$, acting on all but at most two coordinates. The orbits were chosen by maximum-weight independent set search on the orbit conflict graph: branch and bound in the first round, iterated local search in the second. Each code was checked by two separately written programs over all pairs of words and was regenerated from its generators and orbit representatives. We also report two qubit stabilizer codes, $[[20,11,4]]$ and $[[43,32,4]]$, which raise the lower bounds of 3 listed at codetables.de to the listed upper bound 4.

papers.title: Sumsets regularity versus Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for monomial curves
papers.abstract: Let $A=\{0=a_0<a_1<\dots<a_{k-1}=d\}$ be integers with greatest common divisor $1$, let $C_A$ be the projective monomial curve they define, and let $\mathrm{reg}(A)$ be the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of its coordinate ring. Gimenez and Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez proved $\mathrm{reg}(A)\le\sigma(A)+1$ for the sumsets regularity $\sigma(A)$; the reverse inequality $\sigma(A)\le\mathrm{reg}(A)$ was proposed as an open conjecture in a 2024 talk. We show that it fails and measure by how much. Let $c_1,c_2$ be the conductors of the two numerical semigroups attached to $A$ and $N=\lceil(c_1+c_2)/d\rceil$. For curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are not arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, $\mathrm{reg}(A)\ge(c_1+c_2)/d+2$, with equality exactly for the arithmetically Buchsbaum curves, and $\sigma(A)=\mathrm{reg}(A)$. For arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ we prove $9N\le10\,\mathrm{reg}(A)-2$, with $9/10$ best possible, and give an explicit family with $\sigma(A)-\mathrm{reg}(A)$ unbounded. In $\mathbb{P}^4$ a family with a band-shaped Ap\'ery set has $\mathrm{reg}(A)/\sigma(A)\to(2+\sqrt2)/4$ along the solutions of a Pell equation, and gluing carries this bound to every $\mathbb{P}^r$ with $r\ge5$.

papers.title: Bounded powers of edge ideals: Nearly Gorenstein polytopes
papers.abstract: A lattice polytope $\mathcal{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $n$ is called nearly Gorenstein if $\mathcal{P}$ is normal and if its Ehrhart ring is a nearly Gorenstein ring. We study nearly Gorenstein polytopes arising from discrete polymatroids of bounded powers of edge ideals. Especially, it is shown that every nearly Gorenstein polytope coming from either a complete graph or a complete bipartite graph is level.

papers.title: On solutions to tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations
papers.abstract: This paper develops convex analysis on tropical varieties and investigates the properties of the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. We start by introducing notions of plurisubharmonic functions and K\"ahler forms on arbitrary tropical varieties. We show that many classical results of pluripotential theory extend to this setting, including an analogue of Demailly's regularization theorem. Next, we study the solutions to the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. While we establish their uniqueness, we show that the existence is not guaranteed in general. More precisely, we prove that the tropical analogue of the Calabi-Yau theorem fails for any pair $(X, \theta)$ consisting of a compact tropical variety $X$ of dimension at least two satisfying a mild genericity assumption, and a tropical K\"ahler form $\theta$ on $X$. In particular, there exist measures compactly supported in the open part of $X$ that admit no solution. In contrast, for tropical varieties that are regular in codimension one, we show the existence of solutions. Finally, via strongly faithful tropicalizations whose existence is established in this paper, we relate the tropical solutions, when they exist, to the solutions of non-Archimedean Monge-Amp\`ere equations on Berkovich spaces.

papers.title: Terao's freeness conjecture for arrangements of 15 and 16 lines
papers.abstract: We prove that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of 15 and of 16 lines in the complex projective plane. Together with the theorem of Barakat and K\"uhne for at most 14 hyperplanes, this shows that freeness of a central arrangement of at most 16 planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$ is determined by its intersection lattice. The proof has a theoretical and a computational part. Combining published combinatorial criteria for freeness (due to Abe, Dimca, Dimca-K\"uhne-Pokora and Yoshinaga) with Bojanowski's Hirzebruch-type inequality and an elementary counting identity, we show that a counterexample would have exponents $(6,8)$ or $(7,7)$ for 15 lines and $(7,8)$ for 16 lines, and an intersection lattice subject to strong numerical constraints. We then enumerate all 22,544,280 simple rank 3 matroids satisfying these constraints, up to isomorphism, and determine the complex realization space of each of them exactly over $\mathbb{Q}$. Exactly eleven of them are realizable over $\mathbb{C}$, and on each of these the freeness of the realizations is constant. As a by-product we classify the free arrangements of 15 and 16 lines that are not divisionally free, have maximal multiplicity smaller than the smaller nontrivial exponent, and have at least four intersection points on every line.

papers.title: Weights of KZ motives and quantum groups
papers.abstract: The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) connection is defined on the constant bundle determined by $n$ finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a nonzero complex parameter $\kappa$, over the configuration space of $n$ distinct points on the affine line. Work of Schechtman--Varchenko and Looijenga shows that, when $\kappa$ is rational, the resulting local systems admit natural motivic realizations, called KZ motives. The Kazhdan--Lusztig equivalence identifies the local systems underlying these motivic variations with certain representations of the pure braid group arising from the corresponding Lusztig quantum group at a root of unity. We formulate conjectures relating the weight filtrations of KZ motives to structures in quantum-group representation theory, particularly tilting modules and the Jantzen and Andersen filtrations, and provide evidence for these conjectures. Our methods use a new deformation of the representation ring that records the first moments of the weight filtration, together with Schmid's theorem on limiting mixed Hodge structures and results on the Hodge filtration obtained in earlier joint work with S. Mukhopadhyay.

papers.title: James reduced product schemes and double quasisymmetric functions
papers.abstract: Symmetric function theory is a key ingredient in the Schubert calculus of Grassmannians. Quasisymmetric functions are analogues that are similarly central to algebraic combinatorics, but for which the associated geometry is poorly developed. Baker and Richter (2008) showed that $\operatorname{QSym}$ manifests topologically as the cohomology ring of the loop suspension of infinite projective space or equivalently of its combinatorial homotopy model, the James reduced product $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. In recent work, we used this viewpoint to develop topologically-motivated bases of $\operatorname{QSym}$ and initiate a Schubert calculus for $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$ in both cohomology and $K$-theory. Here, we study the torus-equivariant cohomology of $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. We identify a cellular basis and introduce double monomial quasisymmetric functions as combinatorial representatives, analogous to the factorial Schur functions and double Schubert polynomials of classical Schubert calculus. We also provide a combinatorial Littlewood--Richardson-type rule for the structure coefficients of this basis. Furthermore, we introduce an algebro-geometric analogue of the James reduced product construction. In particular, we prove that the James reduced product of a complex (quasi-)projective variety also carries the structure of a (quasi-)projective variety.

papers.title: The Homomorphism Submodule Graph
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a left $R$-module. We define the \emph{homomorphism submodule graph} $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Hom}}(M)$ as the simple graph whose vertices are the proper submodules of $M$, with an edge between distinct vertices $N_1$ and $N_2$ if and only if $\mathrm{Hom}_R(N_1, M/N_2) \ne 0$ or $\mathrm{Hom}_R(N_2, M/N_1) \ne 0$. This graph encodes homological information about $M$ and reflects its internal structure. We compute $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Hom}}(M)$ for semisimple and uniserial modules, establish precise correspondences between graph-theoretic and algebraic properties, and prove that for modules over Artinian local rings, the isomorphism type of $M$ is determined by $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Hom}}(M)$. We also show that over commutative rings with identity, the graph is always chordal, and we relate its spectral radius to composition length in natural families.

papers.title: Directed Hamiltonicity in Generalized Kneser Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical orientation of the generalized Kneser graph $KG(n,k,s)$ contains a directed Hamiltonian cycle for all integers $s \geq 3$ and $n>sk$. Furthermore, we establish that the dichromatic number of this oriented graph is exactly $k$. As a special case, our results apply to the $s$-stable Kneser graphs $K_{s\text{-stab}}(n,k)$, resolving their directed Hamiltonicity and dichromatic number. Our proof adapts the class graph framework of Ledezma and Pastine to the directed setting, leveraging cyclic rotations and friend class adjacencies to construct a single directed cycle spanning all vertices. This work provides a unified and strengthened perspective on the Hamiltonian properties of Kneser-type graphs.

papers.title: Cotangent cohomology and higher-order obstructions of matroids
papers.abstract: Matroid Stanley-Reisner rings admit essential deformation obstructions of arbitrarily high order over every field, already at corank three. For each $m\ge3$, we construct a connected cosimple matroid and $m$ fine-homogeneous first-order classes whose proper subcollections integrate jointly and whose pairwise primary cup products vanish. A specified joint $(m-1)$-jet nevertheless has no lift to order $m$, even without preserving the grading. The construction rests on formulas for every multigraded component of the second cotangent cohomology $T^2$ and of its primary cup image, expressed through flats and parallel classes of the dual matroid. These formulas show that $T^2$ vanishes exactly when every connected component has corank at most two, or equivalently when there is no $U_{1,4}$-minor. This proves a conjecture of Constantinescu, Klein, Nguyen, Singh, and Venturello (2025) and characterizes formal smoothness of the affine deformation functor. For the duals of rank-three truncations of $U_{2,m}\oplus U_{2,n}$, $m,n\ge3$, each nonzero homogeneous class modulo the primary cup image is realized as a higher-order obstruction, and the quotient has an explicit presentation with $m+n-2$ minimal homogeneous generators.
